Name: Vale Config Patcher VCP
Author: valeofhearts
Description:
**WHAT IS IT FOR**

Save all your config files as a patch. So that you can quickly update your config settings with friends, or back them up for yourself.


**WHY THIS EXISTS**

I was setting up a multiplayer game of Stardew, with hundreds of mods.
But something bothered me, if I change a bunch of config settings in my stardew then we have an issue.
I'd have to either manually copy each config file and hope my friends overwrite, or tell them exactly what to update.
Not only would this be tedious, I would definitely wreck everyone's games.

So I got to thinking...
Voila! The VCP is born!

**CREATE A PATCH (START HERE)**

- Run ValeConfigPatcher.bat
- It will prompt you for a Mods path, simply paste it in and press enter.
-The patch is automagically zipped for you so that it's easier to share.
-The config patch will be made in the same location as the script, with the name ConfigPatch_[Date]-[TIME].zip

The other nice thing is it creates an environment variable named [stardew_mods_path].
So if you've already given it a folder, you should be able to just press enter and it should make a new patch automatically!

It should also be portable, and run anywhere on your computer you like. (I haven't tested this in every context. Using it across drive letters may be an issue for some.)


**HOW TO INSTALL A PATCH**

- Unzip it with your program of choice. I recommend 7zip!
-You will want to make sure you have the exact same mods, as whatever each patch was made with! Otherwise you'll end up with extra empty files for mods you don't have. It'll be really confusing and a complete mess.
- Drag and drop the newly extracted Mods folder over your current Mods folder.
- Choose to overwrite all.
- Done!


**ITS BROKEN**

- Regardless of your Mod folder's name the patch folder will always be named "Mods" this keeps things consistent between different stardew installs. You can always unzip and rename if needed.
- Move this folder into your stardew games folder and try again.
- Run as administrator.
- Maybe you have a weird character in your path? like < or & or | or extra spaces, or something else?
- I made this for Windows, if you're using another OS I can't really help. But this is a .bat script, and there may be options for running it through Windows emulators like WINE.
